title: Measurement Schmeasurement: Questionable Measurement Practices and How to Avoid Them
description: General Article in Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science (2020) defining questionable measurement practices as 'decisions researchers make that raise doubts about the validity of the measures, and ultimately the validity of study conclusions', reviewing evidence that measurement reporting is poor, and offering six questions for transparent reporting of measurement (Table 1), beginning 'What is your construct?', 'Why and how did you select your measure?' and 'What measure did you use to operationalize the construct?'.
rightsNotes: The author-hosted PDF opened (media.eiko-fried.com) prints '© The Author(s) 2020' and 'Article reuse guidelines: sagepub.com/journals-permissions'; no Creative Commons statement was found in its extracted text. Free to read, reference-only.
